A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TetHeart study and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables. V2's supplementary Appendices A–G were included, and relocated material can be matched reliably to v1.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction experiments on ACDC, M&Ms and M&Ms-2, clinical-index results, external CHUV and 4DM evaluations, and component ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds configuration sensitivity, slice-position sensitivity and expanded component-ablation results in its supplement.

M1.justification: The tetrahedral representation, attentive feature assembly, shared encoders, GCN–GRU deformation procedure, distillation loss and two-stage training remain equivalent. The default attention neighborhood and deformation iterations are unchanged; supplementary configuration sweeps do not establish a revised proposed method.

E1.justification: The datasets and reconstruction tasks are retained; CHUV is renamed iCMR, also called iMRI. Table S3 adds evaluation of single-slice inputs displaced toward the apex or base on M&Ms, extending the tested spatial input conditions beyond its previous central-slice evaluations.

E2.justification: The sparse-input, full-stack, clinical-index and 4DM comparisons retain their respective comparator sets. FFD, dDemons, 4DMR, MR-Net, MR-Net with nnU-Net, MulViMotion, DeepMesh and the representation variants have unchanged participation in corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces controlled AFA-neighborhood sweeps with accuracy and FPS measurements, plus a seven-position slice-offset protocol. Existing benchmark splits, central 1-/5-slice settings, preprocessing, metrics and 300/150-epoch training schedules remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V1's component ablation covers M&Ms myocardium. V2 substantially expands this analysis with AFA configuration versus accuracy/speed testing (S2), input-position sensitivity (S3), and component ablations across myocardium, LV and RV on all three training datasets (S4).

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without run/seed counts, uncertainty intervals or significance tests. V2 removes Table I's explanation that standard deviations were omitted for space, but the actual statistical reporting practice remains unchanged.

E6.justification: All values in v1 Tables I–V match v2 Tables 1–4 and S1. Tables S2–S4 add supporting results, including M&Ms single-slice myocardium CD of 9.76 mm² centrally versus 15.76 and 12.22 at offsets -3 and +3, configuration-specific accuracy/FPS, and broader ablation scores.

T1.justification: The deformation formalization and learning equations remain equivalent after renumbering. Appendix A.3 supplies standard formulas for already-used metrics, rather than introducing new theoretical definitions, assumptions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The central novelty, unified sparse/full-stack operation and state-of-the-art claims remain. The conclusion modestly tempers clinical translation: v1 says the breakthrough shifts reconstruction to live clinical use, whereas v2 says it has the potential to do so.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands applicability and limitations discussion. Appendix G explicitly acknowledges the sparse/full-stack performance gap and the absence of quantitative iCMR ground-truth validation. Appendices D and F add qualified clinical-index interpretation, slice-selection guidance, and explanations of configuration-related accuracy/speed tradeoffs.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 newly specifies how clinical indices use predicted ED meshes for TetHeart and ground-truth input meshes for relevant baselines. Appendix F discloses the top-k sorting implementation. Most architecture, optimizer, hardware and acquisition details are retained through relocation; code release remains a future promise.

R1.justification: The same 52 cited works are retained despite reordered references and expanded bibliographic formatting. The positioning against contour-based reconstruction, full-stack motion methods and real-time MRI limitations remains substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 extensively condenses and reorganizes the narrative into a shorter main paper and Appendices A–G. It rewrites the introduction and conclusion, separates real-time MRI related work, moves substantial experimental documentation into the supplement, and changes the title, affiliations and dataset terminology.

P2.justification: V2 changes the document template and display sizing, adds the offline-versus-interventional schematic in Figure 1 and Tables S2–S4, relocates the full-slice visualization and 4DM table, and supplies enlarged duplicates of existing motion figures as S1 and S3.

improvement.justification: The added sensitivity tests and broader ablations strengthen evidence for design choices and practical slice selection. Explicit clinical-validation limitations and clearer metric calculations improve transparency. These are incremental gains: the method and principal results remain unchanged, and quantitative interventional validation and statistical uncertainty remain unresolved.
